_comment: Amazon UK root category IDs for Strategy 1, harvested from live product
payloads (categoryTree) rather than typed from a browse-node list.
These are ROOT nodes. Keepa's categories_include matches subcategories, so
a root scopes the scan to a coherent slice without needing a full leaf
tree. Narrow to leaves later once a root proves productive -- the leaf id
is in every candidate's payload, so that costs nothing to discover.
`enabled` reflects whether a root is worth scanning for PRIVATE LABEL, not
whether it sells. Most disabled ones are excluded by the negative filters
anyway; scoping them out server-side saves the tokens instead of spending
them to be rejected locally. An unscoped scan returned 37 rejects from 50.
rotate: 2 enabled categories per night (PLAN.md section 5); the cursor
lives in the SQLite meta table so a missed night resumes in place.

categories.name: Home & Garden
categories.why: Commodity homeware is the classic private-label target: no compliance regime, light, cheap to make, weak incumbents.

categories.name: Stationery & Office Supplies
categories.why: Unregulated, light, high-repeat. Desk organisers and similar are exactly the shape the brief describes.

categories.name: Pet Supplies
categories.why: Large and commoditised. Avoid pet FOOD (FSA regime) -- the compliance filter catches it locally.

categories.name: DIY & Tools
categories.why: Hand tools and fixings are unregulated and durable. Mains-powered items are excluded by the UKCA filter.

categories.name: Sports & Outdoors
categories.why: Accessories (straps, mats, bottles) are manufacturable. Apparel is sizing-and-returns hell; avoid at leaf level.

categories.name: Automotive
categories.why: Accessories and organisers. The jockey-wheel candidate from the first scan sits here.

categories.name: Business, Industry & Science
categories.why: Thin B2B listings with weak presentation and low review counts; under-served on listing quality.

categories.name: Lighting
categories.why: Mains-powered and battery products dominate: UKCA and hazmat. Revisit only for non-electrical fittings.

categories.name: Toys & Games
categories.why: Under-14 safety testing, and dominated by licensed IP. The brief excludes it and the filters agree.

categories.name: Fashion
categories.why: Sizing, returns, and heavy brand gating. Not a first-time-seller category.

categories.name: Beauty
categories.why: CPSR requirement. Explicitly out of scope per CLAUDE.md.

categories.name: Health & Personal Care
categories.why: FSA for supplements, medical-device rules for the rest. The CPAP cushion that slipped through the first scan came from here.

categories.name: Grocery
categories.why: FSA regime, short shelf life.

categories.name: CDs & Vinyl
categories.why: Media: cannot be manufactured. Returned vinyl records on the first unscoped scan.

categories.name: DVD & Blu-ray
categories.why: Media: cannot be manufactured.

categories.name: PC & Video Games
categories.why: Media plus platform gating (Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox).

categories.name: Computers & Accessories
categories.why: UKCA, batteries, and brand gating dominate. Revisit for passive accessories only.

categories.name: Electronics & Photo
categories.why: UKCA and batteries.

categories.name: Baby Products
categories.why: Safety regime overlaps the under-14 toy rules; high liability for a first-time seller.

categories.name: Musical Instruments & DJ
categories.why: Thin volume at this price band and heavily brand-driven.
